Frequently asked questions

What is the learner licence (LL) test?

It is the computer-based test you take at the RTO, or online in some states, before you get a learner licence in India. It checks your knowledge of road signs, road markings and traffic rules. The number of questions, the time allowed and the pass mark differ from state to state.

How many questions and what pass mark do I need?

It depends on your state. For example, Gujarat has 15 questions and needs 9 correct answers (the pass mark was lowered from 11 in July 2024), and Kerala moved to 30 questions with 18 needed from October 2025. The mock test on this site lets you choose your state and uses its format. Always confirm the current format with your RTO.

Is this the official RTO test?

No. This is not an official government website. It only contains practice material for the learner's license test and general information on Indian road safety and traffic rules. The question bank source is parivahan.gov.in.

Is this site free?

Yes. It is free to use, with no sign-up and no login required.

How do I get a learner licence in India?

Apply on the Parivahan Sarathi website, choose your state, fill in your details, upload your age and address proof, photo and signature, book your test slot and pay the fee. With Aadhaar you can take the test from home in some states. Otherwise you take it at the RTO. The learner licence is valid for 6 months, and you can apply for the permanent licence after 30 days. See the step-by-step guide on this site.

What is the minimum age for a learner licence?

16 years for a gearless two-wheeler up to 50cc (with guardian consent), 18 years for a motorcycle or car, and 20 years for a commercial vehicle.

Can I practise in Hindi?

Yes. Use the EN / हिन्दी switch at the top to read the whole site in Hindi, and pick Hindi or English as the question language when you start a mock test.

What topics are covered?

The question bank, state-wise mock tests, mandatory, cautionary and informatory road signs, road markings, traffic lights, hand signals by drivers and traffic police, rules of the road, parking and lights, licence rules, offences and penalties, and accident and first-aid basics.
